title: Farabbi2020
description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants who performed cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery to control a Baxter robot arm reaching toward objects. Each participant completed three sessions with first-person and third-person visual feedback conditions, giving 480 trials per subject. Recordings were made with a 32-channel active-electrode system at 250 Hz and support research on BCI and neurorehabilitation.
methods_description: EEG was acquired with a LiveAmp 32 amplifier (Brain Products) and actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (32 EEG channels plus 3 misc) at 250 Hz. Each session had four motor-imagery runs (first-person training and online, third-person training and online) plus a resting-state recording. Each run had 20 left-hand and 20 right-hand trials, and each trial had a 2 s baseline followed by 4 s of imagery with visual feedback.
